chief_complaint: trouble peeing and lower belly pain
hpi_details: 70M presents with 2 days of worsening difficulty urinating. Today he has been unable to pass any urine for 12 hours and has severe lower abdominal discomfort and fullness.
medications: Tamsulosin, newly started over-the-counter cold medicine (Diphenhydramine)

investigation_events.title: Urgent urinary retention assessment
investigation_events.availability_message: Bedside bladder scan and urgent renal function results are now available. Bladder decompression should not be delayed while awaiting blood tests.

core_concepts: Commonly caused by BPH in older men, often triggered by anticholinergic or sympathomimetic medications (like OTC cold meds).
Can cause post-renal acute kidney injury (AKI).
common_misconceptions: Assuming anuria is due to a kidney problem (pre-renal/intrinsic) without checking bladder volume.
dangerous_errors: Failing to decompress the bladder promptly, leading to permanent detrusor damage or severe AKI.
management_principles: Immediate bladder ultrasound, placement of Foley catheter, check BMP for AKI, stop offending meds.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for Kidney Disease

reference_soap.subjective: 70M with BPH presenting with acute inability to void for 12 hours and suprapubic pain after taking cold medicine.
reference_soap.objective: Distended, tender suprapubic mass. Bladder scan shows >999 mL.
reference_soap.assessment: Acute urinary retention, likely medication-induced superimposed on BPH.
reference_soap.plan: STAT Foley catheter placement. Check BMP. Stop diphenhydramine. Follow up with urology.

learning_objectives: Recognize acute urinary retention and identify common medication triggers.

teaching.one_liner: Acute inability to void with a painful, distended bladder in an elderly man, often triggered by anticholinergic medications.

must_ask.say: When did you last pass urine, and how has your urine stream been recently?
Have you had any trouble starting your stream, dribbling, or waking at night to urinate before this?
Have you taken any cold or allergy medicine, or other new medications recently?
How severe is the lower belly pain, and does it come with an urge to void?
Have you had any back pain, leg weakness, or numbness that could point to a nerve problem?
